about: The toolkit's core set of adapters: one per major barrier, each built only on the building blocks (tools/core-adapters/<id>.js), each verifiable. Briefs for the agents run with run.mjs --create (CREATE.md). suggestedFor is only which people onboarding suggests the adapter to first; it never limits who can use it. Adapters have no shortcuts of their own: the toolkit has one pair of keys the person gives to one adapter (s.keys.adjust says what up and down do), and 'every site' is chosen in the extension's popup.

adapters.name: Text size and spacing

needs.description: Makes text bigger, by zooming or by the text size alone, with more space between lines and letters.
needs.abilities: Small or tightly packed text is hard to read: low vision, tired eyes, reading from further away, or reading more easily with more space.

adapters.adjusts: With the person's shortcut (s.keys.adjust, label 'Text size', settings fontScale): up and down change fontScale in steps of 10 percent, 100 to 200, saved for this site and announced. Line and letter spacing follow the person's settings (lineHeight, letterSpacing); they adjust those in their profile.
adapters.brief: Makes text bigger and gives it more room, as the person's settings say. Text size is the browser's zoom or the text size alone, as s.zoom.method() says (the person's textSizeMethod, else the option `method`, default 'zoom'), never both. With the text size alone, scale the page's text (including text sized in px) without breaking layouts: no text cut off, no overlap, no sideways scrolling at 320 pixels. Line and letter spacing follow WCAG 1.4.12 (line height up to 2, letter spacing up to 0.12 em, word spacing 0.16 em, paragraph spacing 2 em when asked) with nothing cut off or overlapping. Applies once, in enable(); does nothing on a page when no setting asks for it (returns false) unless the person adjusts it there. The text size alone is s.text.scale (the block measures and never compounds). Where no setting asks for anything it keeps running and changes nothing (no zoom call at all: the person's own browser zoom stays), so the shortcut can adjust it there. Spacing is one stylesheet. Spacing goes through s.text.fit(() => s.css(...)), which grows only the boxes the spacing made cut text off; s.text.scale already does the same for size. Never read every element's height yourself, and never change a box the page cuts off by design (a teaser, a truncated card), on load or later. Turning a spacing setting off takes its stylesheet away; letterSpacing 0 asks for no spacing (no word spacing either). Size first, then spacing. Each setting the person can turn off (spacing, the text size) lives in its own s.group(): turning it off is that group's end(). Paragraph spacing comes with any spacing setting. Back at 100%, forget what was scaled.
verify: the text is at the person's fontScale (computed sizes of body text, headings and px-sized text), by zoom or by text size, never both
with textSizeMethod 'zoom', zoom is set to fontScale/100 and put back on disable(); with 'font', zoom is never touched
WCAG 1.4.12 spacing applied with no text cut off (no element's scrollHeight above its clientHeight where it was not before)
no sideways scrolling at 320 pixels wide
the shortcut's up and down (__verifyPress('Alt+Shift+ArrowUp')) change the size and save it for this site; nothing is saved without a key press
layout shift happens only at enable(), never later
with no fontScale asked, s.zoom is never called and the page is unchanged; the shortcut's up then makes it 110%
text added after enable() is at the same size, never twice the size
a box the page cuts off by design (fixed height, overflow hidden) is left as it is, with and without settings
with nothing asked, enable() reads no element's layout and changes nothing

adapters.name: Contrast

needs.phrase: Text that stands out from its background
needs.description: Raises the contrast of text that is too faint against its background, or gives pages light text on a dark background.
needs.abilities: Faint or low-contrast text is hard to make out: low vision, color blindness, glare, or bright light being uncomfortable.

adapters.adjusts: With the person's shortcut (s.keys.adjust, label 'Contrast', settings contrastMode): up goes to the next mode (more contrast in the page's own colours, then yellow on black), down to the previous, then off; saved for this site and announced.
adapters.brief: Raises text contrast to at least WCAG AA (4.5:1, 3:1 for large text) where the page falls short, computing colours without AI: measure each text element's colour against its real background (s.page and the colour helpers), and darken or lighten the text colour only as much as needed, keeping its hue. contrastMode 'yellow-black' instead gives every text yellow on black through one stylesheet. Leaves text that already meets the ratio alone, and images, video and canvas untouched. Handles text added later. With no contrastMode asked for, still fixes text below AA (that is its purpose). Use s.page.textContrast(el) for each text element (its fix keeps the hue); measure each element once and fix text added later by itself. Each mode lives in its own s.group(), so changing mode ends that group instead of undoing by hand. The person's darkMode is not the page's background. An element hidden when it is first seen is measured when it is shown, never marked done while hidden. Yellow-black never removes background images (icons and sprites stay) and never styles inside an <svg>.
verify: axe-core color-contrast problems go down and none are added
text that already passes keeps its exact colour
the hue of a fixed colour is kept
yellow-black mode: computed colours of text and backgrounds
new text added after enable() is fixed once, without flicker
the shortcut's up and down change the mode and save it
changing mode with the shortcut and back leaves no colour of the earlier mode behind

adapters.name: Focus and keyboard

needs.description: Shows clearly where the keyboard is on the page, adds a way to skip to the main content, and makes controls reachable with the keyboard.
needs.abilities: A mouse or touch screen is hard or impossible to use, so they use a keyboard, a switch, or voice control that acts like one; or they lose track of where they are on the page.

adapters.adjusts: nothing (the shortcut, if the person gives it to this adapter, turns it on and off; the toolkit does that).
adapters.brief: Makes keyboard use visible and possible: a strong focus indicator on every focusable element (s.highlight focus ring: at least 3:1 against what is around it, never covering the focused element or hiding it under sticky headers), a 'Skip to main content' link that is the first thing Tab reaches and moves focus to the main content, and scroll-into-view of the focused element when the page hides it under a fixed header (WCAG 2.4.11). Never changes the page's tab order or adds tabindex above 0. The skip link is s.focus.skipLink() (none is added where the page has one that works) and keeping focus out from under fixed bars is s.focus.keepVisible(): one scroll, never two. Count only what a person can focus (not disabled, not type=hidden, not tabindex -1, not contenteditable=false); a page with none of those and no main content has nothing to do. Test enable() itself on a page that has its own skip link. A tabindex is negative when its number is below 0 (parse it). The option `to` may be an element or a selector. Write a test page of its own with a working skip link, and check that enable() there adds none.
verify: every focusable element shows a visible indicator of at least 3:1 when focused (sample several, including ones with outline: none)
the skip link is first in tab order, visible when focused, and moves focus to main
a focused element under a fixed header is scrolled into view
no tabindex above 0; tab order unchanged
nothing added covers the focused element
on a page with its own skip link, no second one is added

adapters.name: Bigger targets

needs.description: Makes small links, buttons and form controls bigger to hit, with room between them.
needs.abilities: Small targets are hard to hit: a tremor, limited hand control, a pointer held in the mouth or on the head, or a large touch screen used with fingers.

adapters.adjusts: With the person's shortcut (s.keys.adjust, label 'Target size', settings targetSize): up and down step targetSize through 24, 32, 44 pixels, saved for this site and announced.
adapters.brief: Makes small links, buttons and form controls at least targetSize CSS pixels (default option 24, WCAG 2.5.8; 44 is WCAG 2.5.5) to hit, measuring first and changing only what is too small. Prefer growing the hit area without moving anything (padding with negative margin, or a larger hit area on a pseudo-element), so the page reflows at most once at enable(); inline links in running text get spacing that keeps lines readable. Never shrinks anything, never covers a neighbouring target. Measure each interactive element once (links, buttons, form controls and elements with an interactive role, not every element on the page) and grow only those too small; handle ones added later by themselves. A new targetSize redoes the sizes in a new s.group(), never by clearing and redoing on each change of the page. Nothing outside its job (no focus styles). Elements added later come in batches (s.watch.added with { batch: true }): measure the batch and the targets near it once, then change them; never measure every target on the page for each one added. A target inside a focusable or clickable container is still a target; skip only one inside another link or button. Where padding cannot grow the box (border-box with a fixed size, overflow hidden), grow its hit area another way and check the size it reached. A <label> is a target only when it labels a control, and never both it and its control. Nothing too small, or bigTargets off: nothing to do. Every kind of target reaches targetSize at any size asked for (24, 32, 44), checkboxes and radios too, and controls that are positioned absolutely or fixed, and SVG controls (their hit area from an HTML element around or over them). Neighbours are what is near on screen, not only siblings, also for what is added later. Leave the page's pointer-events alone. Return false when nothing is too small.
verify: each interactive element measures at least targetSize in both dimensions (getBoundingClientRect, or its hit area)
axe-core target-size problems go down
layout shift under 0.1
no two targets overlap after the change
inline links in a paragraph stay readable (line height not doubled)
the shortcut's up and down step the size and save it
a change of the page (an element added) does not redo the sizes of the others
adding 200 links later takes one pass, not one per link (enable and the later pass stay well under a second on a long page)

adapters.name: Page structure

needs.description: Gives the page regions and headings that a screen reader or a keyboard can jump between.
needs.abilities: They move through pages by structure rather than by looking: they use a screen reader, or find long pages without clear parts hard to follow.

adapters.adjusts: nothing (the shortcut, if given, turns it on and off). The outline opens from a 'Page outline' button that is the first thing Tab reaches after any skip link, visible when focused, so it covers nothing.
adapters.brief: Gives the page a structure people can navigate by: adds missing landmarks (main, navigation, banner, contentinfo) with ARIA roles only where the page has none and the region is unambiguous, and an outline of the page's headings in a panel (s.panel) opened from a 'Page outline' button, where choosing a heading moves focus to it and closing gives focus back. Never changes headings' levels or text. The 'Page outline' button is s.focus.entry({ label: 'Page outline', onActivate }). Give a landmark role only to a div or section, never to a list (ul, ol) or a native element. A header or footer inside an article, section, aside, main or nav is not the page's banner or contentinfo: it neither counts as one nor stops a region from being the main content. End the session before enable() returns false. Banner and contentinfo candidates follow the same rule as header and footer: not inside an article, section, aside, main or nav. Take the outermost candidate, never a part of it. A copyright line alone does not make a footer. Nothing to do (no landmark to add and no outline asked for): return false. Give headings ids only when the outline is opened.
verify: landmarks added only where missing; axe-core region and landmark problems go down, none added
the outline lists the headings in order, with levels
choosing one moves focus to that heading; Escape closes the panel and focus returns
the panel never covers the content it points to; it has a name and a Close button

adapters.name: Announce changes

needs.phrase: Hear about changes on the page
needs.description: Tells a screen reader when the page changes without saying so: a message that appears, new content, a new view.
needs.abilities: They use a screen reader, so a change they cannot see goes unnoticed unless it is announced.

adapters.adjusts: nothing (the shortcut, if given, turns it on and off).
adapters.brief: Tells screen reader users about changes the page makes without saying so: a status or error message that appears, content that replaces a region, and a single-page app moving to a new view (s.watch.route), when the page does not already announce them (aria-live, role status or alert). One short, plain announcement per change, through s.announce, never for the adapter's own changes or the toolkit's UI, and never a flood (batch, and skip changes the person caused by typing). On real pages most changes are not messages: timestamps and counters that update, tickers, carousels, ads, infinite lists, lazy images. Announce only what reads as a message: a new element whose role, class, id or name says status, alert, error, notice, message, toast or similar, or content that appears or replaces a region within a few seconds of the person's own action (a click, a key, a submit). Never text that changes inside existing content on its own, never content outside the viewport, never iframes. No selectors for any one site or test page. The toolkit's UI is what s.page.isOurs says; never skip content by a part of a class name or id. Typing in a text field, Space and Enter included, is typing, not an action. A route change is one announcement (the new view's heading), not also its content. <output> is a live region. A message added while the page's own live region has just spoken is announced after it, not dropped. A ticker is its container updating again and again, whatever nodes it adds. Timers: s.timer returns a function that cancels it. A ticker is the same container updated again and again (count per container). After a route change, the new view's content is not an answer to the click that navigated. A new element that is itself role status or alert is announced; one added inside an existing live region is not. A message inside a new container is still found. Cancel a pending route announcement when another route change comes.
verify: a message added to the page is announced once (the shared live region's text)
a change inside an existing aria-live region is not announced twice
a route change is announced with the new view's heading or title
the adapter's own and the toolkit's changes are not announced
a burst of 20 changes gives at most a few announcements
a timestamp that updates itself every second is never announced
on real sites, while a person scrolls and does nothing else, it says nothing or nearly nothing

adapters.name: Calm page

needs.description: Stops what moves on its own: animations, smooth scrolling, autoplaying video and moving images.
needs.abilities: Movement makes it hard to focus or is uncomfortable: distraction, dizziness or nausea from motion, sensitivity to busy pages.

adapters.adjusts: nothing (the shortcut, if given, turns it on and off).
adapters.brief: Stops what moves on its own: CSS animations and transitions, smooth scrolling, autoplaying video and GIF-like animated images (paused with a visible way to play), auto-advancing carousels (paused, and their controls kept), and marquee-like scrolling. Through s.media and one stylesheet. Content stays visible in its final state. Nothing it paused starts again on disable() unless it was playing before; anything the person plays or starts themselves stays as they left it. For a carousel, use its own pause or stop control when it has one (WCAG 2.2.2); otherwise hold the slide shown, and if the page puts it back more than a few times, stop holding it rather than fight the page. Measure once: never read the scroll width of every element on the page. Click a carousel's own control only when it is inside the carousel (aria-roledescription carousel, or a region or group whose name says carousel or slideshow), its accessible name says pause or stop (not its class), it is a button that is not a submit button and not in a form, and the carousel is playing (its name or aria-pressed says so). Never click anything else on the page. When holding a slide, change only the slides (the track's own children) and only their state; never another element's classes. Say nothing on load. Read classes with getAttribute('class') (an SVG's className is not a string). Holding a slide moves only its state class (active, current, selected and the like), through the session. Never pause CSS animations with animation-play-state (they stop at their first frame): end them in their final state. On disable(), a carousel paused with its own Pause button is started again with its own Play button (or the same button when it toggles). A play is the person's only when their input was on that media or its own controls. Every feature off: nothing to do. One carousel is handled once, even when its inner parts' classes also say carousel. A disabled Pause button means the carousel is not playing: leave it. On disable(), start again only a carousel this adapter paused. The options for animations and transitions are separate. Leave Web Animations as they are (only the stylesheet and s.media). Pause each media element once; s.media.pause is safe to call again.
verify: computed animation and transition durations are none or 0 after enable()
an autoplaying video is paused, with controls; a muted looping one too
a carousel stops advancing (its slide stays the same for several seconds)
content hidden by an animation start state is visible
disable() restarts only what was playing
a video the person plays after enable() keeps playing
no button outside a carousel is ever clicked, even one named Stop or Pause next to a slider
nothing is announced on load

adapters.name: Captions on

needs.description: Turns on the captions and subtitles that videos and audio already have.
needs.abilities: Speech in videos and audio is hard to hear or follow: deaf or hard of hearing, a noisy or quiet place, or following better when reading along.

adapters.adjusts: nothing (the shortcut, if given, turns it on and off).
adapters.brief: Turns on the captions that videos and audio already have: for each media element with a captions or subtitles track, shows the one in the page's (or the person's browser's) language, else the first, through s.media.captions; including media added later. Leaves media with no track alone and says nothing about it. Never starts playback. The earlier track states come back on disable().
verify: a video with a captions track in the page's language has that track showing
with two tracks, the matching language is chosen
media added later gets its captions on
a video without tracks is untouched
track modes return to what they were after disable()
nothing starts playing

adapters.name: Names for controls and images

needs.phrase: Names for buttons, fields and images
needs.description: Gives buttons, links and form fields that have no name a short one, and images that have no description one.
needs.abilities: They use a screen reader or voice control, which cannot say or reach a button, field or image the page left unnamed.

adapters.adjusts: nothing (the shortcut, if given, turns it on and off).
adapters.brief: Gives buttons, links and form fields that have no accessible name a short one, and informative images that have no alt text a description, with s.ai.text('label', …) from the control's context and s.ai.vision('describe', img, { purpose: 'alt' }). Measures first (s.page's accessible-name helper): never renames anything that has a name, never describes decorative images (tiny, spacer, role presentation) — leaves those alone or marks clearly decorative ones alt="" only when certain. Asks the AI once per element, at most a limited number per page (an option, default 20), never for content the page hides. Answers are checked by the blocks; on null, leaves the element as it was. Name from the page first, without AI: a title, an svg title, the words of an icon's class or image file name, the link's last path part, a nearby label. AI only for what is still nameless, visible ones first, at most the limit per page (default 10); images only when informative (larger than 48 by 48 pixels and not decorative). The person pays for every call on every page they visit. A file name's words name only a small icon (48 by 48 pixels or smaller); a photo or illustration is never named from its file name (on null from the AI, it is left as it was). Words from a class or file name match whole words (btn-dislike is not 'Like'); style words (primary, secondary, btn, icon, large) are not names. A link to '#…' or '?…' is never named from the page's path. A label next to a field names it only when it labels nothing else (a label for another field is that field's). Mark an image inside a named control alt="" only when it is small or clearly decorative. An <input type=image> with alt has a name; a field whose only label is empty does not. An image is informative when either side is over 48 pixels. An element's own title names it. s.watch.added with { batch: true } hands an array; name the controls inside added content too. Spacer images are tiny (2 pixels or less), never by a word in the address. File-name words come from the last part of the path only, never from a data: URI or a host. An image with only width or height set is measured by what is set. Read classes with getAttribute('class'). An element that already has a name (s.page.nameOf) is left alone, images included. A label beside fields names only the field right after it. Directions (left, right, up, down) are part of a name. Only the session this enable() made may be ended by it.
verify: axe-core button-name, link-name, label and image-alt problems go down, none added
controls that already had a name keep it exactly
with AI unavailable (no answers) nothing changes and enable() still applies cleanly
with fixed answers, the names are set as aria-label or alt
decorative images are not sent to the AI
at most the limit of AI calls on a page with many unnamed controls
on a real page, no AI call for a control the page names in some way the page-first rules find
a large photo with a descriptive file name is not given its file name as alt text

adapters.name: Plain language

needs.description: Offers each long or hard paragraph again in plain language, at their reading level, when they ask.
needs.abilities: Long sentences and unusual words are hard to follow: reading in a second language, dyslexia, memory or attention, or wanting the point quickly.

adapters.adjusts: nothing in the profile (reading level is a profile field, not a setting); the person chooses which parts to simplify.
adapters.brief: Lets the person read a long or hard paragraph in plain language at their reading level, on request: a small 'Plain language' button after each long paragraph in the main content (or one button for the section they are in), which replaces that paragraph with the simplified text (s.ai.text('simplify', …), s.text.replaceBlock) and becomes 'Show original', one click back. Never simplifies on load and never sends more than the paragraph asked for. Keeps names, numbers, dates and links' meaning (the prompt's `keep`); on null leaves the paragraph and says it could not. While a request is on its way, the button keeps focus: aria-disabled and aria-busy, never disabled (Chrome moves focus to the page). With many long paragraphs (more than 8), one button per section instead of after each. End the session before enable() returns false. With sections, each long paragraph belongs to exactly one button: the innermost section or article, and paragraphs outside every section get one of their own. Acronyms (all capitals) go in keep. In a section, a paragraph the AI could not simplify stays as it is, and the button still toggles the others back without asking again. Paragraphs outside every section each get their own button after them. Keep day-first dates and short month names; do not keep a capitalized first word of a sentence.
verify: buttons appear only after long paragraphs in the main content, as real buttons with names
clicking one replaces that paragraph with the answer and the button toggles the original back, with aria-pressed or a changed name
no AI call happens on load
with AI unavailable, clicking says it could not and leaves the paragraph
the person's readingLevel reaches the request
layout shift on enable() under 0.1

adapters.name: Read aloud

needs.description: Reads the main content or the text they select aloud, highlighting each word as it is spoken.
needs.abilities: Reading text on a screen is tiring or slow: dyslexia, low vision, fatigue, or understanding better by listening.

adapters.adjusts: speechRate with Slower and Faster buttons in its control bar (steps of 0.1, 0.5 to 2), and with the person's shortcut (s.keys.adjust, label 'Speech rate', settings speechRate): up faster, down slower. Saved for this site and announced.
adapters.brief: Reads the main content (or the text the person selected) aloud on request, highlighting each word as it is spoken (s.speech.say with onWord and s.highlight). Starts only from its own Play button, never on load; Escape stops it; a small control bar (Play/Pause, Stop, Slower, Faster) placed so it covers nothing the person is reading. Speech is the browser's own in the runtime. Skips navigation, the toolkit's UI and hidden text. No 'every site' button: the person chooses that in the extension. Announce the rate set() actually applied. A rate change while speaking goes on from the current word at the new rate. Read a selection with s.speech.say(selection) so its words are highlighted too. A rate change restarts once, from the current word (s.speech.say(el, { from })), in s.profile.onChange; a rate changed while paused is used when the person plays again. No readable text: nothing to do. The bar adds to the page's own bottom padding instead of replacing it.
verify: nothing is spoken on load
Play (a trusted click) speaks the main content's text, not the navigation
the person's speechRate is used
words are highlighted as they are spoken and the highlight goes on stop
Escape stops it; Pause and Play resume
Slower/Faster and the shortcut's up/down change the rate and save it for this site
the control bar's buttons have names, are 24 pixels or more, and cover no content
